articles.title: Microsoft quiere preservar juegos de Xbox y ha elegido una vía inesperada: emularlos oficialmente en Windows
articles.text:
La industria del videojuego avanza con una rapidez que no siempre deja espacio para mirar atrás. Llegan nuevas consolas, las tiendas se renuevan y el formato físico pierde terreno, mientras una parte del catálogo antiguo queda vinculada a sistemas, cuentas y servicios que no duran para siempre. Quienes hemos intentado volver a un juego de hace décadas sabemos que conservarlo no significa necesariamente poder ejecutarlo. Ese es el punto en el que la preservación deja de ser solo una preocupación de archivos y museos.
En ese contexto, Microsoft ha elegido una fórmula poco habitual para recuperar parte de su historia: llevar juegos de la primera Xbox a Windows 11 sin convertirlos en remakes ni en versiones nativas para PC. La firma estadounidense asegura que este lanzamiento marca el inicio de un esfuerzo más amplio de preservación, aunque, como veremos, estamos ante una prueba limitada. También hay otro detalle que cambia la magnitud del anuncio: la vía técnica por la que estos juegos pueden funcionar en hardware actual. Veamos.
La primera Xbox empieza a encontrar una nueva vida en Windows
Por ahora, el programa no abre todo el catálogo histórico de Xbox ni permite ejecutar cualquier juego antiguo en Windows. El punto de partida no es una colección amplia, sino cuatro juegos concretos con los que Microsoft comienza a trasladar una parte de la historia de Xbox a Windows. La empresa no ha detallado todavía qué títulos llegarán después ni a qué ritmo crecerá el catálogo. De momento, estos son los elegidos:
- 'BLiNX: The Time Sweeper'
- 'Conker: Live and Reloaded'
- 'Crimson Skies: High Road to Revenge'
- 'Fuzion Frenzy'
Como decimos, lo que llega a Windows no son remasterizaciones convencionales ni adaptaciones rehechas juego por juego. Según confirmó Microsoft a PC Gamer, Xbox utiliza emulación para reproducir en un ordenador moderno el entorno necesario para ejecutar software diseñado para su primera consola. Esa solución mantiene la jugabilidad original, pero permite añadir mejoras como VSync, un reescalado de resolución de hasta cuatro veces, filtrado anisotrópico y antialiasing reforzado. Los usuarios también pueden elegir entre los modos de pantalla completa y ventana, además de configurar el idioma y el audio.
La iniciativa tampoco se limita al ordenador de sobremesa. Los títulos pueden instalarse en dispositivos portátiles compatibles con Windows 11, incluidos ROG Xbox Ally y ROG Xbox Ally X, sin depender obligatoriamente del juego en la nube. Los requisitos mínimos son modestos para el hardware actual: 8 GB de RAM, un Core i3-8100, Ryzen 3 1200 o Ryzen Z2 A, y gráficos equivalentes a una GTX 950, Radeon RX 550, Intel UHD 770 o Arc A310.
Desde una perspectiva favorable, el avance resulta difícil de ignorar. Microsoft está prolongando la vida útil de obras que hasta ahora permanecían ligadas al hardware de Xbox y a su sistema de retrocompatibilidad en consolas posteriores, y las acerca a jugadores que quizá nunca tuvieron aquellas máquinas. El problema aparece cuando pasamos de conservar el acceso a conservar una copia. Microsoft no ha anunciado instaladores independientes ni versiones sin DRM, el sistema utilizado para controlar y verificar las licencias digitales. Tampoco ha detallado qué comprobaciones exigirán estos cuatro juegos, cuánto tiempo podrán funcionar sin conexión o si seguirán disponibles para descargar dentro de, por decir una cifra, diez años.
Sí sabemos que su acceso depende de Windows 11, la aplicación Xbox y una licencia vinculada a nuestra cuenta. Es una diferencia importante frente a GOG, que permite descargar instaladores de respaldo sin DRM y guardar los archivos para instalarlos sin utilizar su aplicación.
Todo esto ocurre mientras la industria reduce las vías independientes de acceso a sus catálogos. Nintendo cerró en marzo de 2023 las compras digitales de Wii U y Nintendo 3DS, aunque mantiene por ahora la posibilidad de volver a descargar el contenido adquirido. Sony, por su parte, ha anunciado que dejará de producir discos para todos los juegos nuevos de PlayStation desde enero de 2028. Son dos decisiones diferentes, pero ambas recuerdan que la disponibilidad de una obra digital depende en último término de la continuidad de una plataforma y de las condiciones que establezca su propietario.

articles.title: Exclusive: StrongestLayer raises $4.1M for reasoning-based email security - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Exclusive: StrongestLayer raises $4.1M for reasoning-based email security
Artificial intelligence-based email security startup StrongestLayer Inc. revealed today that it has raised $4.1 million in new funding to expand its platform and go-to-market push ahead of a planned Series A round.
Founded in 2024, StrongestLayer offers software that skips the signatures, reputation databases and past-attack patterns that most email security relies on. Instead, it reads a message and works out the intent behind it, then rules on whether the note is genuine or built to deceive. The company said that lets it flag attacks it has never encountered, since the call rests on context, not a prior match.
The target is a class of threats that slips past older products. StrongestLayer said it examined thousands of detections at customer sites from December through February and found that pattern-matching and behavioral filters, the backbone of most email security, could not reliably catch more than a third of the attacks landing in inboxes.
Many of the costliest ones carry no malicious link or attachment. A business email compromise or an executive impersonation scam can be in plain text, written to read as legitimate so that a person acts on it.
“Every generation of email security was built to recognize attacks it had seen before,” said Alan LeFort, StrongestLayer’s co-founder and chief executive. “That worked when attackers reused templates and infrastructure. It does not work when every attack is unique. We didn’t build a better filter. We built a system that reasons about whether a message is legitimate and whether it intends harm.”
StrongestLayer said production deployments have grown more than eightfold since its first round a year ago and that the platform has beaten both legacy secure email gateways and newer AI-branded rivals in competitive evaluations. Its threat research, including a taxonomy of 44 email attack subtypes, is posted at tools.strongestlayer.org.
Inovia Capital Inc. led the new round. Existing investor Sorenson Capital returned, joined by new backers LaunchPod, Alumni Ventures Group and Chris Key, former chief product officer of Mandiant. Taha Mubashir, a partner at Inovia, said the firm invested because the startup had done more with less. StrongestLayer reached a point where it could challenge entrenched vendors on a fraction of the money such companies usually spend to reach the market, he said.
Sorenson also led the company’s first round, a $5.2 million raise announced in July 2025. StrongestLayer has now raised $9.3 million in total.

articles.title: IA da OpenAI escapa de teste e ataca Hugging Face • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
IA da OpenAI escapa de teste e ataca Hugging Face
Modelo GPT-5.6 Sol e IA inédita burlaram restrições e invadiram servidores da Hugging Face sem intervenção humana.
Modelo GPT-5.6 Sol e IA inédita burlaram restrições e invadiram servidores da Hugging Face sem intervenção humana.
A OpenAI admitiu nesta terça-feira (21/07) que seus próprios modelos de IA conseguiram escapar de um ambiente de testes, conectaram-se à internet e invadiram sozinhos os sistemas da plataforma Hugging Face. O ataque cibernético “sem precedentes”, segundo a empresa, ocorreu neste mês e foi motivado por um objetivo simples: encontrar a resposta para uma avaliação de cibersegurança.
O incidente foi detectado pela plataforma invadida. De acordo com a OpenAI, a invasão foi desencadeada por uma combinação de algoritmos operando em conjunto, incluindo o recém-lançado GPT-5.6 Sol e uma IA ainda mais avançada, em fase de pré-lançamento.
A “fuga” aconteceu depois que os modelos identificaram e exploraram uma vulnerabilidade de dia zero (uma falha crítica ainda sem correção) em um software usado dentro da OpenAI durante uma avaliação interna para medir as capacidades de segurança das ferramentas.
Para testar os limites em um cenário extremo, a desenvolvedora removeu intencionalmente as travas de segurança e filtros de proteção dos modelos em um ambiente que deveria ser 100% isolado, o que deixou as IAs hiperfocadas em resolver o desafio a qualquer custo.
Elas realizaram um escalonamento de privilégios e vasculharam a infraestrutura da empresa até encontrarem um nó da rede (uma máquina específica) com acesso à web. Já conectados à internet, os algoritmos fizeram uma dedução lógica: a Hugging Face, famosa por ser um dos maiores repositórios de códigos do mundo, provavelmente abrigava a resposta para a sua avaliação.
A partir desse ponto, o modelo disparou múltiplos vetores de ataque e explorou brechas, usando até credenciais roubadas na nuvem para executar códigos remotamente. O ataque cibernético só foi interrompido porque a Hugging Face também usa IA para proteger sua própria rede. O sistema de detecção de anomalias da plataforma notou o tráfego suspeito, isolou as ações e bloqueou a atividade antes que um estrago irreversível acontecesse.
Apesar do susto, a Hugging Face confirmou que não encontrou evidências de adulteração em bancos de dados de parceiros, modelos de clientes ou espaços públicos. As falhas usadas como porta de entrada foram corrigidas, as credenciais vazadas acabaram revogadas e o caso foi repassado às autoridades.
A OpenAI, por sua vez, também implementou configurações mais rígidas em seus servidores internos, reportou a falha de dia zero aos desenvolvedores do software afetado e trabalha em conjunto com a Hugging Face nas investigações.
Segundo o CEO da Hugging Face, Clem Delangue, o avanço das ameaças autônomas exige uma mudança de postura da indústria: “A segurança da IA não será resolvida por uma única empresa trabalhando em segredo. Ela será resolvida de forma aberta, colaborativa, com amplo acesso à IA para todos”.

articles.title: Samsung Announces Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Fold8, and Flip8
articles.text:
Wednesday, July 22nd 2026
	
		
	
	
	Samsung Announces Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Fold8, and Flip8
Samsung Electronics today unveiled the new Galaxy Z series, its most complete lineup yet, designed to expand foldables to a wider audience. The lineup introduces Galaxy Z Fold8, a fresh and exciting form factor that provides a new kind of foldable experience built around the way people explore, discover and immerse themselves in their favorite content.
The lineup also includes Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, which brings Galaxy's renowned Ultra standard to foldables with maximum productivity and content creation in a larger workspace. Galaxy Z Flip8—the sleekest one yet—was built for expression and quick interaction on the go. Built on seven generations of foldable innovation and consumer insight, the new Galaxy Z series gives users more choice than ever, with three distinct experiences engineered to fit different needs.Galaxy AI has been optimized for each of these form factors. Across the lineup, every insight feels more actionable and every action feels more connected. Multitasking is easier on the larger screens of Galaxy Z Fold8 and Fold8 Ultra, while Flip8's AI-native FlexWindow keeps relevant information and shortcuts within reach. And with partner AI experiences such as Gemini Intelligence, Galaxy gives users even more ways to get things done in fewer steps—with transparency, privacy and user control built in.
"As AI becomes more agentic, mobile devices will become the most personal entry point to experiences that understand and adapt to each user," said TM Roh, Chief Executive Officer, President and Head of the Device eXperience (DX) Division at Samsung Electronics. "By setting a new standard for foldables, we are once again advancing the premium mobile experience and opening the next era of intelligence to more people."
The All-New Galaxy Z Fold8: A New Galaxy Fold Experience for Everyday Immersion

articles.title: Vibe-Coding in drei GTA-Spielen: So hat ein Modder die Spielwelten miteinander verbunden
articles.text:
Drei GTA-Spiele in einem: So hat ein Modder die Spielwelten per Vibe-Coding verbunden
Während viele Gamer:innen weiterhin gespannt auf GTA 6 warten, vertreibt sich ein Modder die Zeit in den alten Ablegern der Reihe. Der User, der auf X und Github als „dryxio“ unterwegs ist, hat ein besonderes Projekt in GTA 3, San Andreas und Vice City gestartet. Er wollte die drei riesigen Spielwelten der Open-World-Hits miteinander verbinden.
So funktionieren die GTA-Portale
Wie der Modder in einem ersten Clip zeigt, scheint ihm dieses Vorhaben jetzt gelungen zu sein. Das Video startet in GTA: San Andreas. Direkt in der Grove Street finden sich nicht nur CJ und seine Gang wieder, sondern auch drei große, leuchtende Portale. Eines davon führt in die Welt von Vice City, ein anderes zu GTA 3, während das letzte Portal zu einem anderen Punkt in San Andreas springt.
Das Beeindruckende daran ist, dass es sich nicht nur um statische Aufnahmen der Spielwelten handelt und beim Durchgehen das andere Game gestartet wird. Es handelt sich stattdessen um in Echtzeit berechnete Welten, die sogar auf die Aktionen aus anderen GTA-Welten reagieren. Sobald ein Portal durchschritten wird, wechselt die Spielwelt und auch der gesteuerte GTA-Charakter nahtlos.
Wie „dryxio“ schreibt, laufen alle drei Spiele dafür gleichzeitig in einem Prozess und teilen sich die Rechenleistung des PCs. Sobald Spieler:innen von einer GTA-Welt in die andere wechseln, übernimmt die jeweilige Engine des Zielspiels die Kontrolle über den laufenden Prozess. Im Hintergrund bleiben die anderen Engines aktiv und warten darauf, wieder am Drücker zu sein.
Ebenfalls beeindruckend: Jedes Spiel innerhalb des Prozesses behält die eigenen Einstellungen, Speicherstände und Missionen bei. GTA-Spieler:innen könnten also in San Andreas eine Mission absolvieren und dann direkt nach Vice City springen, um eine andere Aufgabe innerhalb der Story anzugehen. Die Verbindungen können mit einer Portal-Gun frei in der Spielwelt gesetzt werden.
Laut Forenbeiträgen auf Resetera wurde das Projekt mit KI-Hilfe realisiert. Allerdings ist noch nicht ganz klar, welches Tool dafür genutzt wurde. Das liegt daran, dass der Modder sein GTA-Werk noch nicht öffentlich gemacht hat. Der Clip war wohl nur ein kleiner Ausblick auf den Release. Wann genau die Dateien auf Github veröffentlicht werden, ist nicht bekannt. Sobald das passiert, könnten aber auch alle anderen Gamer:innen, die alle drei Spiele besitzen, die Portale ausprobieren.

articles.title: Así es como al resolver Captcha has ayudado a entrenar la IA de los vehículos autónomos
articles.text:
El sencillo gesto de seleccionar imágenes de autobuses, semáforos o tractores en un captcha puede convertirse en información que ayude, sin saberlo, a entrenar sistemas de inteligencia artificial.
Este proceso ha sido clave para el avance de tecnologías como los vehículos autónomos, cuyos sistemas requieren grandes volúmenes de datos etiquetados por humanos para funcionar de manera eficiente, según un informe de El País.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo los captchas son usados para entrenar a la IA
Los captchas, esas pequeñas pruebas que exigen identificar objetos en imágenes o marcar una casilla para demostrar que no eres un robot, no solo sirven como filtro contra el tráfico automatizado. Empresas como Google han aprovechado su masificación para recolectar y etiquetar imágenes de forma automática y a gran escala.
El uso de estos datos generados por los usuarios, eligiendo correctamente las imágenes con autobuses, por ejemplo, ayuda a etiquetar la base de datos y a que el software aprenda a identificar estos objetos, algo fundamental para filiales como Waymo, dedicada a los vehículos autónomos.
PUBLICIDAD
Por qué los captchas son claves para los vehículos autónomos
Seleccionar imágenes correctamente permite alimentar conjuntos de datos esenciales para entrenar sistemas de reconocimiento de objetos. Estas bases, que suelen estar relacionadas con el tráfico, vehículos y señales, son indispensables para el desarrollo de automóviles capaces de circular de manera autónoma.
La catedrática Karina Gibert de la Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya explica que la mayoría de los captchas utilizan imágenes relacionadas con el tráfico por la necesidad de los coches autónomos de reconocer obstáculos, señales y otros vehículos.
PUBLICIDAD
De esta manera, cuando los usuarios etiquetan correctamente, por ejemplo, un tractor borroso, el sistema aprende a identificar patrones incluso en condiciones adversas como lluvia o suciedad en la cámara.
Para entrenar un sistema de visión por computador, se requieren algoritmos de aprendizaje supervisado que trabajan sobre bases de datos etiquetadas. Los captchas generan estas bases de alta calidad, que crecen constantemente y permiten que los algoritmos reconozcan semáforos o señales desde cualquier ángulo y bajo distintas condiciones ambientales.
PUBLICIDAD
La evolución de captcha y el valor de los datos para la IA
El desarrollo de los captchas lo logró Luis von Ahn, quien en los años 2000 creó el sistema reCAPTCHA para proteger sitios web del tráfico automatizado y también para ayudar a digitalizar libros antiguos. Los usuarios contribuían al identificar palabras difíciles de descifrar, facilitando así la conversión de textos impresos a formato digital.
En 2009, Google adquirió reCAPTCHA y amplió su funcionalidad, adaptándolo tanto para la protección contra bots como para la digitalización masiva de libros y periódicos. Esta expansión permitió a la compañía entrenar algoritmos capaces de leer textos con mayor precisión, aprovechando la intervención humana en el etiquetado.
PUBLICIDAD
Durante un tiempo, Google comunicó de forma explícita que los captchas cumplían una doble función: servían como herramienta de seguridad y, a la vez, como fuente de datos para mejorar sistemas de inteligencia artificial. Las imágenes y textos que los usuarios ayudaban a identificar pasaban a formar parte de conjuntos de datos empleados en el entrenamiento de modelos de aprendizaje automático.
En 2018, la empresa anunció que con la llegada de la versión 3 de reCAPTCHA dejó de utilizar los desafíos visuales para el entrenamiento de modelos, enfocándose en optimizar la protección de los sistemas.
PUBLICIDAD
Sin embargo, muchas páginas web aún funcionan con versiones anteriores que sí permitían el uso de datos para tareas de aprendizaje automatizado. Además, existen dos versiones del servicio: una orientada a empresas, con un marco claro de uso de datos, y otra gratuita, en la que las condiciones de privacidad han sido más generales.
El valor estratégico de los datos generados por captchas ha sido resaltado por especialistas, como Jordi Nin, quienes consideran que constituyen un recurso clave para perfeccionar algoritmos de reconocimiento, fundamentales para sectores como el de los vehículos autónomos.
PUBLICIDAD
En abril de 2026, Google actualizó su política y pasó a actuar como procesador de datos, transfiriendo la responsabilidad principal a los propietarios de las páginas web que implementan el sistema, bajo condiciones más estrictas y transparentes para el tratamiento de la información.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Windows 11 : Microsoft s'attaque enfin à la vénérable fenêtre Propriétés
articles.text:
Windows 11 : Microsoft s'attaque enfin à la vénérable fenêtre Propriétés
Elle n'avait pas changé depuis Windows 7. La petite fenêtre qui s'affiche quand on fait clic droit > Propriétés sur un fichier s'apprête enfin à adopter le look moderne de Windows 11.
Clic droit, Propriétés : le geste est ancré dans la mémoire musculaire de quiconque a un jour manipulé un fichier sous Windows. Pourtant, la fenêtre qui s'ouvre n'a pratiquement pas changé depuis deux décennies. Ce statu quo touche peut-être à sa fin. Phantomofearth, développeur habitué à fouiller les entrailles du système, a repéré dans la build Insider la plus récente une version modernisée de cette boîte de dialogue, entièrement reconstruite en WinUI 3.
Une première apparition discrète dans la Corbeille
Pour l'instant, la nouvelle interface ne se montre que dans un recoin précis : les propriétés d'un fichier placé dans la Corbeille. Coins arrondis, typographie actualisée, respect natif du mode sombre : le résultat tranche nettement avec la fenêtre classique, restée figée dans l'esthétique héritée de Windows 7.
Le périmètre limité de cette apparition suggère que Microsoft procède par étapes, comme elle l'a fait avec la barre de commandes, la page d'accueil ou le volet de détails de l'Explorateur de fichiers, tous trois déjà portés vers WinUI 3 au fil des mois.
Le chantier K2 en toile de fond
Cette modernisation s'adosse à l'initiative interne baptisée "Windows K2", dont l'ambition affichée est de corriger les irritants les plus tenaces de Windows 11. La fragmentation visuelle du système figure en bonne place sur la liste : il suffit d'ouvrir les Paramètres, puis de basculer vers le Gestionnaire de périphériques, pour constater que deux époques cohabitent sur un même écran. Microsoft a confirmé plus tôt cette année vouloir porter le menu Démarrer et l'ensemble des applications intégrées vers WinUI 3, tout en optimisant les performances du framework lui-même pour éviter toute régression de fluidité.
Aucune date de déploiement grand public n'a été communiquée. La présence de ce premier indice dans les canaux de test laisse toutefois entrevoir une arrivée dans les prochains mois.

articles.title: Microsoft announces Xbox Backward Compatibility for PC — will let gamers play classic console games on PCs and handhelds
articles.text:
Microsoft announces Xbox Backward Compatibility for PC — will let gamers play classic console games on PCs and handhelds
Including the new Xbox ROG Ally lineup
Xbox has announced a new Xbox Backward Compatibility for PC program, which will let gamers play a selection of classic Xbox titles on PCs and handhelds, a move the company says marks the beginning of a bigger push into Xbox game preservation. The announcement begins with four titles that can now be played on PCs and handhelds, including the ROG Xbox Ally and Ally X.
"This marks the beginning of a broader effort to preserve XBOX games from the past and bring them to PC over time," the company said in a blog post authored by Xbox "VP next generation" Jason Ronald. Alongside backward compatibility, the company says games will also include new features. The four titles in the announcement are:
You can now buy all of these games on PC, and they're also included in all Xbox Game Pass plans. Anyone who already owns these titles digitally on console can also now play them on PC or handheld, with support for Xbox Play Anywhere and Xbox Cloud Gaming. Crucially, this appears to be a digital-only preservation effort, so it won't help anyone who only owns physical copies of these games. Xbox has reportedly been testing a way to digitize physical games as far back as Xbox One, but that hasn't yet materialized yet.
Alongside the preserved original gameplay, Xbox claims these games will let users customize graphics settings, with up to 4x resolution scaling, VSync support, Fullscreen and Windowed modes, anisotropic filtering, and enhanced anti-aliasing, with more features to come in the future. Notably, Xbox will add achievements to select original Xbox games on console and PC.
Users who want to play these titles will need to meet the following system requirements:
| Spec: | Minimum requirements | Recommended specs | 
| GPU | Nvidia GTX 950 or AMD Radeon RX 550 or Intel UHD 770 or Intel Arc A310 | Radeon RX 68005 or Nvidia GTX 1070 Ti or Intel Arc A770 | 
| CPU | Min 4 Cores Intel Core i3-8100 or AMD Ryzen 3 1200 or AMD Ryzen Z2 A Processor | 6 cores and 12 threads Intel Core i5-10400 or AMD Ryzen 5 3600 or AMD Ryzen AI Z2 Extreme | 
| RAM | 8GB | 8GB | 
| DirectX | N/A | DirectX12 API, Hardware Feature Level 11 | 
| OS | Windows 11 | Windows 11 | 
| Drivers | Latest Version as of January 2026 | Latest Version as of January 2026 | 
Microsoft's emphasis on preserving older games is particularly noteworthy given recent backlash against Sony over its decision to end physical games with its next console generation, and the shuttering of some of its online stores. While Xbox's digital emphasis on game preservation still can't match the solidarity of physical media preservation, the timing of this announcement seems like more than just a coincidence.

Stephen is Tom's Hardware's News Editor with almost a decade of industry experience covering technology, having worked at TechRadar, iMore, and even Apple over the years. He has covered the world of consumer tech from nearly every angle, including supply chain rumors, patents, and litigation, and more. When he's not at work, he loves reading about history and playing video games.

Galaxy Watch Ultra com design robusto volta a cair 65% para Dia dos Pais 2026
Galaxy Watch Ultra tem corpo de titânio resistente e tela AMOLED brilhante, assim como o novo Galaxy Watch Ultra 2; smartwatch é ótima opção para presente
Galaxy Watch Ultra tem corpo de titânio resistente e tela AMOLED brilhante, assim como o novo Galaxy Watch Ultra 2; smartwatch é ótima opção para presente
O Galaxy Watch Ultra LTE de 47 mm está saindo por apenas R$ 1.736 no Pix no Mercado Livre. O smartwatch da Samsung com tela AMOLED até 3.000 nits e proteções IP68 e 10 ATM está com 65% de desconto sobre o preço original de R$ 4.999, logo após a chegada do novo Galaxy Watch Ultra 2.
Comprando ainda hoje, o relógio inteligente chega a tempo para ser o presente desse Dia dos Pais 2026.
O Galaxy Watch Ultra possui corpo de titânio com suporte das certificações IP68 e militar MIL-STD-810H, que resiste a até 100 metros de profundidade (10 ATM). O sucessor entrega uma certificação parecida (10 ATM+), e ambos smartwatches são habilitados para uso na água doce, clorada ou salgada.
A tela Super AMOLED de 1,5″ entrega brilho de até 3.000 nits, capaz de reproduzir imagens nítidas e com cores vivas, além de garantir a visibilidade em qualquer ambiente. O relógio inteligente é similar ao novo Watch Ultra 2, com este tendo uma tela mais brilhante de até 5.000 nits.
Seu sensor principal BioActive e os auxiliares suportam diversas atividades esportivas, como ciclismo, caminhada e corrida. E oferecem recursos avançados de qualidade de vida, como eletrocardiograma (ECG), monitores do sono, da saúde da mulher e da oxigenação do sangue.
O chip é um Exynos W1000, enquanto o modelo recém-lançado vem com Snapdragon na ficha técnica pela primeira vez em um Galaxy Watch. Já a RAM de GB e os 64 GB de armazenamento permanecem os mesmos e permitem a execução local de aplicativos.
A bateria também mudou entre as gerações, com o Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 oferecendo componente 35% maior. Porém, os 590 mAh do Galaxy Watch Ultra já resistem até 100 horas de uso segundo a Samsung, com o modo de economia de energia ativado.
O relógio ainda é compatível com Wi-Fi 5, Bluetooth 5.3 conectividade LTE/4G e GPS multibanda, podendo determinar a posição do usuário em tempo real. Graças a estes recursos, o Galaxy Watch Ultra (por R$ 1.736 no Mercado Livre) ainda é uma das melhores opções para quem quer comprar um smartwatch.

articles.title: DAC 2026: DIY AI Is Now in Vogue; Users Are Not Waiting - EE Times
articles.text:
When my friend Simon Davidmann, whose framework anchored Part 1 of this series, laid out his agentic AI argument in recent months, one observation got less attention than his band-aid-versus-reset headline, yet it deserves more: The customers are doing it themselves. Hyperscalers and semiconductor houses are not waiting for vendors to ship finished AI products. They are building their own orchestration, their own agents, and their own models, on top of the simulation, formal, implementation, and signoff engines they already license. The EDA tools become engines; the intelligence layer above them increasingly belongs to the user.
As Simon pointed out, Samsung, Nvidia, and their peers are assembling internal AI stacks that treat vendor tools as engines beneath a domain-specific intelligence layer. But he attached a barbed caveat: Because that work stays behind corporate firewalls, it is “effective and myopic at the same time.” Each giant rebuilds similar integrations in private; the lessons never propagate to the rest of the industry—and, worse for the rest of us, the giants get to learn from all their own data, something those outside the walls can only wish for. That is Davidmann’s Dilemma from Part 1 in its purest form: every player acting rationally and the ecosystem collectively worse off for it.
If you want evidence that DIY AI is now mainstream practice rather than hyperscaler exotica—and, contra Simon’s caveat, that at least some of the lessons are starting to propagate in public—the DAC 2026 Engineering Track is the closest thing we have to proof. An honest qualifier belongs here: The most secretive giants still are not presenting—you will not find Nvidia, Meta, or OpenAI walking through their internal design-AI stacks, and some of the industry’s most advanced users treat their flows as IP and stay home entirely. What the Track shows is the visible part of the iceberg. But the visible part has grown remarkably.
The Engineering Track is DAC’s user conference within the conference—working engineers presenting deployed results, peer-reviewed by other engineers—and this year, it reads like a census of do-it-yourself AI. What follows is my tour of the DIY AI wave, followed by its deliberate juxtaposition: users adopting the vendors’ AI, with equally concrete numbers. Both are true simultaneously, and the tension between them is exactly where Simon’s framework earns its keep.
Exhibit A: Samsung teaches an RL agent to tune an SoC
Start with the presentation I would use to explain the entire trend to a skeptic: On Monday morning, Samsung Electronics engineers Hyungtae Park, Rira Oh, Sanggu Kim, Hyunjae Woo, and Youngsik Kim present “Adaptive QoS Optimization for SoC Performance Enhancement Using Dueling Double Deep Q-Networks.” The problem: Modern SoCs expose a thicket of quality-of-service knobs—arbitration, priorities, bandwidth allocations across many masters—and manually tuning them across varying scenarios has become intractable. Samsung’s answer: Build an execution environment that runs the SoC pre-silicon—think emulation—and set a reinforcement-learning (RL) agent loose in it. The agent—Deep Q-Networks with dueling and double-DQN enhancements, prioritized experience replay, the full modern RL toolkit—explores the design space against reward functions built on throughput, latency, and power and discovers QoS settings that significantly outperform manual methods.
Notice the architecture of the achievement—and notice, per Part 1’s model-spectrum musing, that there is no LLM in sight: This is a user-trained optimization model, not a wrapped chatbot. The execution infrastructure that makes the exploration trustworthy comes from the EDA world; the intelligence that exploits it is Samsung’s own, purpose-built for Samsung’s architectures and Samsung’s performance targets for what they call “System Performance Verification.” That division of labor—vendor engines below, user intelligence above—is Simon’s observation rendered as a methodology paper, and it repeats across the track.
The DIY AI census
IBM turns agents loose on verification debug—and on tool development itself. In IBM Z hardware verification, agentic flows now automate failure triage and root-cause analysis, integrating design specifications, HDL, waveforms, coverage data, and prior issues through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, with customized agents extracting cone-of-influence logic and correlating transactions—reporting an estimated 15% to 40% reduction in manual effort on one of the most expertise-hungry tasks in the flow.
A second IBM paper goes a level more meta: an agentic framework that generates EDA utilities themselves from user specifications using reusable MCP building blocks, reducing one structural-verification tool’s development from an estimated four person-weeks to under 30 minutes. Note MCP appearing twice: The connective-tissue standard from Part 1’s data-and-glue layer (where Perforce pairs it with RAG for design-data context) is showing up in user methodology papers barely a year after entering the conversation. The connective tissue is arriving. And it raises a question Simon put to me directly, worth carrying into Tuesday’s Build-versus-Buy panel: Why are the big EDA vendors not shipping these utilities themselves—and why are users such as IBM building rather than buying from the startups next door?
An on-premises LLM babysits emulation regressions
A flagship-SoC team from Samsung presents an unattended software-testing framework for pre-silicon emulation that pairs fast-boot virtualization with an on-premises LLM that reads kernel panics and decides: genuine software bug or non-critical bring-up artifact? The detail to savor is “on-premises”—the confidentiality requirements of semiconductor design mean the user’s DIY AI runs inside the user’s walls, on top of the vendor’s emulation platform. Another team presents an on-premises, multi-agent “Team of Experts” pipeline—a classifier agent routing to specialized sub-agents for UVM code generation, log parsing, and specification retrieval across JEDEC, LPDDR, and HBM documents—built with RAG and finetuning precisely so that no design data leaves the building.
The knowledge layer gets formalized
A Samsung team presents an ontology-driven knowledge graph that transforms hundreds of pages of interlinked design documents into a queryable graph feeding a Graph-RAG chatbot—the specification-engineering thread from Part 1’s front-end stage, implemented by users for users. In the POWER processor verification environment, ML-driven analysis correlates test components with coverage events and composes “super-tests” that make up 86% of recommended test cases for hard-to-hit scenarios.
Implementation and analog join in
Texas Instruments describes a deep-RL analog sizing tool—with custom reward shaping, optimizing across all PVT and Monte Carlo corners—deployed at scale with over 100 circuits optimized to signoff quality. An automotive SoC team from Renesas presents a Random Forest framework predicting die size from design specifications with R2 up to 0.95 across 1,800 RTL modules. On the Gladiator stage, a team from Samsung uses LLMs to interpret netlists and cluster DRAM peripheral cells for placement—expert structural knowledge written as natural-language prompts rather than rule-based code—cutting design-rule violations by 80.6%, while Samsung’s Sungsu Byun applies gradient-boosted models to switch-cell optimization against RedHawk-reported voltage variation. A neuro-symbolic framework presented by Cadence called Auto-Chk compiles natural-language signoff intent into deterministic checkers—120+ checklist items in production, 20× faster checker development. Even formal verification gets the treatment: AI-generated “helper” invariants converting bounded proofs into full closure. And one paper turns AI on the infrastructure itself, using graph neural networks and RL to forecast EDA compute needs, cutting cloud overprovisioning by 60% to 80%.
Add it up, and the pattern is unmistakable: RL agents, on-prem LLMs, knowledge graphs, multi-agent pipelines, neuro-symbolic compilers—built by users, running on vendor engines, presented with deployment numbers rather than aspirations. Hold each one up to Davidmann’s Test, and the census gets even more interesting: Most of this speeds up what their teams already verified—dramatically, honestly, and with numbers. A few—the invariants that convert bounded proofs into full closure, the QoS exploration no human team could have swept—edge toward changing what can be verified at all.
The juxtaposition: vendor AI, adopted and audited
Now let’s look at the other half of the picture, because the same Track that documents the DIY AI wave also documents users adopting vendor AI—and, in the best Engineering Track tradition, auditing it in public.
A user methodology paper on Cadence Voltus InsightAI examines AI-driven power-grid reinforcement for IR closure—and does something refreshingly honest: It presents a detailed design-impact analysis for working with the tool’s capabilities and around its limitations. That sentence is the Engineering Track’s entire value proposition in miniature. Broadcom’s APD AI team and Synopsys’s RedHawk-ET team jointly present an early 3DIC thermal flow, correlated to silicon within 3°C (Part 3 returns to it)—vendor AI and user expertise co-developed rather than bought off the shelf. Intel presents its library QA framework built on Siemens’s Solido Crosscheck, native checks fine-tuned alongside custom ones. An AI-driven thermal-aware placement methodology explores hundreds of constrained scenarios for 3D chiplet stacks. And in the special sessions, Sandisk’s Mariana Shenker shows production AI workflows for specification-driven development—the user-experience counterpart to the “Spec-Tacular!” session’s startup pitches.
So which is it: users building their own or users adopting the vendors’? The Track’s answer is both, sorted by where the intelligence needs to live. Where the problem is deeply proprietary—an SoC’s QoS behavior, a company’s debug tribal knowledge, confidential failure logs—the AI is homegrown and on-premises, with vendor engines supplying the physics and the simulation truth underneath. Where the problem is common to everyone—IR closure, library QA, thermal analysis—vendor AI embedded in the platforms wins on economics. The boundary between those two zones is, I suspect, where the next five years of EDA business models get decided. Simon’s holistic reset, if it comes, will have to serve both sides of that line; Monday’s DAC Pavilion panel “Agentic AI in EDA: Who’s in Control?” and Tuesday’s “Build vs Buy: Who Owns the Intelligence Behind Tomorrow’s Chips?” put that exact question on stage, and Simon himself joins Wednesday’s exhibitor forum panel, “Harnessing AI for SoC Verification: Disruptive or Collaborative?”—the perfect closing argument for this article’s thesis, argued live.
For the startup-side complement to these user stories, Monday’s Veriest-hosted exhibitor forum session, “Beyond the Hype: Innovation in AI for Chip Design and Verification,” showcases what the agentic layer from Part 1’s landscape is building for exactly these users.
The itinerary, complete
Three parts, one arc: Part 1, the landscape of who; Part 2, the users quietly building their own intelligence on the industry’s engines; and Part 3, the sessions on creating AI chips—the end product this whole industry exists for.
And if Part 1’s Expedia comparison did not convince you, here is a culinary one: Think of DAC Explorer as the conference’s AI sous-chef. Hand it the ingredients you fancy: say, a base of RL, some on-premises LLMs, and a pinch of MCP, and it finds the recipe—a personalized schedule of sessions, plated and ready to export. No reservations are required, although seats at the popular sessions do go fast.
Registration is at dac.com, and every session mentioned here is in the official DAC 2026 program. See you in Long Beach.
Frank Schirrmeister writes about semiconductors, EDA, and system design. He serves as program chair of the DAC Engineering Track; this series is written in that capacity, not on behalf of his employer, Synopsys. Opinions are his own.

articles.title: LG Display Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results
articles.text:
Wednesday, July 22nd 2026
	
		
	
	
	LG Display Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results
LG Display today reported unaudited earnings results based on consolidated K-IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) for the three-month period ending June 30, 2026.
For the second quarter of 2026, the company recorded revenues of KRW 5.61 trillion and an operating loss of KRW 107.7 billion.
The first half is traditionally a slower season for the display industry, as set manufacturers adjust component inventories ahead of new product launches in the second half of the year. In addition, the second quarter reflected one-off expenses associated with workforce efficiency measures.
Despite these factors, LG Display improved its first-half operating results by KRW 121.6 billion compared to the same period last year, successfully minimizing the impact of seasonal demand weakness and one-time costs. The performance reflects tangible progress in advancing its OLED-centered business portfolio based on its technology leadership.
In the second half of the year, LG Display plans to further strengthen its business competitiveness by securing best-in-class technologies and advancing technology-driven cost innovation. In particular, beyond conventional cost reduction efforts, the company will maximize efficiency across the entire value chain - from development and manufacturing to production - through technology innovation centered on AI Transformation (AX). LG Display thus aims to fundamentally enhance its business structure and sustain growth by delivering differentiated customer value.
In its small and mid-sized business, the company will strengthen its competitiveness by focusing on high-end products built on its differentiated technological advantages. At the same time, it plans to respond flexibly to changing market conditions by maximizing its stable technology, development, and mass production capabilities.
In its large-sized business, LG Display will further expand its leadership in the premium market by leveraging a product lineup that combines differentiated technologies with cost competitiveness. As the monitor market continues to transition from LCD to OLED, the company plans to strengthen its portfolio of high value-added products, including Gaming OLED monitor panels, while expanding shipment volumes.
"Excluding one-time factors, our underlying business profitability stayed positive in the second quarter," said Sung-hyun Kim, CFO of LG Display. "In the second half, we will continue improving our annual performance by advancing cost innovation and further strengthening our business competitiveness, while establishing a more stable and sustainable profit structure."

articles.title: I'm a big Marvel fan — these are the MCU movies and TV shows I want to hear more about at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, including the new X-Men film
articles.text:
Power on... Marvel at San Diego Comic-Con 2026 — and what the comic book giant could show after the Avengers: Doomsday trailer's earlier than expected release
The 2026 edition of San Diego Comic-Con (SDCC) is almost upon us, and you know what that means: all manner of rumors and speculation about the surprises Marvel might have in store for us at its now-customary Hall H panel.
To a certain extent, the biggest reveal has already happened. Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) diehards had expected the first official trailer for Avengers: Doomsday to be the focal point of the comic book titan's next presentation. With Avengers: Doomsday's main trailer released on Monday (July 20), though, Marvel must have something just as significant around which to center its forthcoming panel on July 25 at 5:30pm PT.
As attentions turn towards the Disney subsidiary's hour-long address at SDCC 2026, chief among fans' immediate thoughts is: what big reveal could Marvel make that a) would rival Avengers: Doomsday's first proper trailer as a major talking point, and b) is so noteworthy that Marvel felt confident enough to unveil Doomsday's trailer earlier than expected?
One project that fits the bill is Marvel's new X-Men movie. The only post-Multiverse Saga film in active development, myriad rumors are circulating online about who could star in the mutant-led flick. You can learn more about which actors Marvel is reportedly talking to via my Marvel's X-Men movie guide.
For what it's worth, industry insiders, albeit ones with sketchy track records, have claimed there'll be no such cast reveals at SDCC 2026. My reading of the situation is that'll be the case, too, especially as Marvel will want to focus to stay on the rest of its 2026 line-up — I'll discuss this in more detail shortly — and the projects it'll release in 2027, such as Daredevil: Born Again season 3 and Avengers: Secret Wars. We're not expecting the new X-Men movie to arrive until the following year.
That said, I'd be surprised if Marvel doesn't say something about the MCU's first X-Men film. Speculation abounds that the comic titan might tentatively discuss other Marvel Phase 7 movies, such as Thunderbolts 2, The Fantastic Four: First Steps sequel, Black Panther 3, Nova, and Midnight Sons — the last of which might repurpose Marvel's long-gestating plans to introduce Mahershala Ali's Blade to the MCU. It would be bizarre, then, if that quintet is covered, but not the first film of what'll be version 2.0 of the MCU.
But, onto more pressing matters — namely, the rest of Marvel's 2026 movie and TV slate.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
On the film side of things, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which swings into theaters between July 29 and 31 (depending on where you live), is expected to have a big presence at SDCC 2026. I'm willing to bet that attendees will be treated to some exclusive first-look footage, but any spoiler-based content, such as the identity of Sadie Sink's much-discussed mystery character in Spider-Man 4, won't be part of proceedings. Could we also get an early Spider-Man 5 announcement? As a huge Spidey fan, I'd be overjoyed if we did.
As for Avengers: Doomsday, I believe Marvel will show off some new clips from one of this year's most anticipated new movies, with the most likely candidates being extended looks at shots from its first main trailer. Where its sequel in Secret Wars is concerned, I think we'll get a name-drop and the briefest, spoiler-free hints about its story, but that's all.
Pre-SDCC 2026 chatter about Marvel's forthcoming Disney+ shows is much harder to read. After all, the studio has regularly reserved its biggest TV announcements for D23 Expo (Disney's flagship fan event, which takes place annually in Anaheim, California), so it stands to reason that there won't be a change in strategy this year.
Nevertheless, I predict we'll get some details about its final two TV series of the year — VisionQuest and Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man (YFNSM) season 2 — at SDCC.
With VisionQuest, I foresee confirmation of its main cast and a behind-closed-doors look at the Paul Bettany-led live-action program. Whether that'll be a full first trailer or a more general sneak peek remains to be seen, but I wouldn't be surprised if, as long as it's the former, VisionQuest's first trailer isn't publicly released following its possible unveiling at SDCC.
The same is true of YFNSM season 2. I'm of the opinion that Marvel's animated Spider-Man show will be highlighted in greater detail at D23 Expo 2026. That said, I'm fairly confident that Marvel will also deliver some news about it. Is it too much to ask for an official launch date? Not in my book.
Meanwhile, Marvel has already confirmed that it's full steam ahead on season 3 of its critically-acclaimed animated series X-Men 97. Will we hear more about it shortly? Not in my view. We've still got three more episodes of X-Men 97 season 2 to enjoy before it goes off the air, so any conversations about its follow-up season — especially those of a spoiler-based persuasion — will have to wait until D23 Expo 2026 or this year's New York Comic-Con.
Finally, will we hear anything substantial about Wonder Man season 2? That's similarly unlikely. Co-creator Destin Daniel Cretton has been incredibly busy with directing Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Although Cretton recently said that the cameras could roll on Wonder Man's next chapter as early as next year, this year's D23 Expo feels like a better fit for any major announcements for this series, as well as Marvel Zombies season 2, the company's first R-rated animated program.
What Marvel movies and TV shows do you think we'll see and hear more about at SDCC 2026? And which one(s) are you most looking forward to? Let me know in the comment section below and the above poll you probably scrolled past.

articles.title: Altera CEO Raghib Hussain's First Year - EE Times
articles.text:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. — A little over a year since taking over as Altera CEO, and nine months after gaining independence from Intel, Raghib Hussain’s dogged focus on execution is transforming into measurable results. The company has taped out six chips in three months (three ahead of schedule), is growing “in the 20% range,” and has reduced RMAs (return merchandise authorization, or product returns) by 60%, Hussain told EE Times.
Nine months ago, Hussain told EE Times he wanted to focus on execution, and he has done exactly that.
“I am super-pleased with our progress on execution,” he said. “Full independence was needed to implement our culture, our style, without anyone telling us what to do. I’m super happy with our Silverlake partnership, which gives us full freedom to do the right thing for the business.”
The team is working to fill some holes in the product roadmap, and Altera’s next generation is also being properly defined and executed, he said.
“Last year, we did six tape-outs, which is not normal for Altera,” he said. “When you bring the right people and give them the right target and push them to achieve, they do actually step up. As I always say: There are no bad engineers, only bad management.”
Engineers need direction, and they need motivation to push the limits, but that is now happening at Altera, he said. Three of Altera’s six tape-outs were ahead of schedule.
“This is huge engineering execution and discipline progress,” Hussain said. “Execution was one of the biggest challenges for Altera in the last few years.”
Portfolio development usually takes five to seven years. Altera is bringing it closer to three years, Hussain said. Tape-outs are expensive, but Silverlake understands the value of engineering investment and ROI, he added.
Moving from Intel to being a smaller company has meant less bargaining power in parts of the supply chain, but Hussain said the team anticipated memory shortages and stockpiled several years’ worth of DRAM. Moving fast on this decision is another advantage of being a private company, he said.
Internal culture
Execution begins and ends with internal culture, and this is something Hussain has had to change rapidly from the top down.
“I wanted to have a culture which is more customer-focused, with a growth mindset,” he said. “Mindset drives behavior. I want everyone to think about the purpose of our existence, which is to solve customer problems using FPGAs. If everyone starts thinking from that point of view, half the problem is solved automatically.”
The new culture should also include a “yes, we can” attitude, Hussain said. People at large companies are very risk-averse, he said, which drags everything down.
“[With a ‘yes, we can’ attitude] maybe 30% of the time you cannot, because it’s not physically possible, but there is another 30% of the time where you will get things done which you would not have attempted otherwise,” Hussain said.
That mindset has to be driven from the top, he said, noting that he has brought in a new leadership team, hiring not just FPGA veterans but people from across the industry, provided they have the right mindset.
“They should not be working for the paycheck—they should have a passion for what they are doing, and they should be an expert in their functional area,” he said. “With that in mind, I have hired people from five or six different companies.”
Hussain said he personally interviewed at least 20 people for each position, such is the critical nature of getting these appointments right.
Hussain has also eliminated half the levels of internal hierarchy—there were previously as many as 12 levels in some parts of the business.
[Separately, Altera employees told EE Times that Intel’s multiple layers of bureaucracy had been problematic, but the faster pace at which Altera operates and makes decisions is evident throughout the business.]
The hardest thing about rewriting internal culture is eliminating the old culture, Hussain said. The belief internally was that Altera couldn’t tape out a chip in less than four years, but similar tape-outs elsewhere in the industry can be done in less than a year.
“The toughest thing was opening up people’s eyes and giving them belief that we can do it—that belief actually is the starting point,” Hussain said.
For Altera’s first next-generation product, the first tape-out completed under Hussain’s watch, the team said it would take 18 months. “We did it in nine months, two weeks,” he said.
Altera’s current product line is already in production, far ahead of its 2027 target.
“We also introduced new parts which will go to production by the end of this year, which tells you how we are trying to drive the pace,” Hussain said.
Becoming independent
Since formally separating in September, Hussain has moved quickly to sever ties with Intel. Of the 125 transitional service agreements (TSAs) the company had with its former parent, 110 have since ended, Hussain said. Many of the completed agreements covered internal IT systems and software, buildings, and facilities. Some of the remaining agreements relate to engineering compute platforms, where the switchover requires careful timing consideration to minimize disruption. All TSAs should be complete in the next few months, he said.
“Large corporations which have been around for a long time have lots of baggage,” Hussain said. “Every 10 years, we should reset the company.”
A reset, similar to moving house, should prompt questions about “do we really need this?” he said. “It’s difficult, but that forces you to do a lot of the right things that you should have done anyway.”
Resetting the company gives the team a chance to deploy the latest technologies and techniques, adopt AI in internal processes, and implement new systems in some places, he said.
Customer trust
Altera is working hard to reestablish trust with its customers.
“We are here, we are focused on FPGA, we are not going to get distracted or deprioritize FPGA for something else,” Hussain said. “That’s our focus, and it is shown in our progress—we already achieved 68% of our design win goals for 2026.”
Customer interaction has been improved through an intentional restructuring to remove layers between the customer and Altera’s engineers.
“When I came in, there were four or five layers between the customer and final engineering,” Hussain said. “Many times, things didn’t even get to our engineering teams, so they didn’t know the actual issues. Throughout my career, I have worked very closely with the customer because unless you do that, you won’t understand the real problem, and once you understand the real problem, you can find a solution.”
Altera now has reduced internal organizations to two: sales support and engineering. This has brought engineering conversations directly to the customer, which has helped the team prioritize its roadmap.
So far, feedback has been excellent, and customers are much more engaged, Hussain said.
Hussain also likes to visit customers personally, “especially the difficult ones,” he said. Some potential customers have not used Altera in 10 or 15 years, but it’s these customers who provide the most valuable feedback.
“The response I’m getting is very good—they are saying, finally, Altera is back!” he said. “Altera is paying attention to what we are looking for, and Altera has intentions to solve our problems in the next generation. This is very refreshing for them.”
A stronger Altera that can offer customers a real choice is a benefit, he added.
Results
The hard work is paying off. Revenue grew in the 20% range last year and will be similar this year, Hussain said, noting that the company is “very profitable” and has doubled its cash balance position since becoming independent.
This growth is down to wins for existing products, while revenue for new products addressing previously unserved market segments such as robotics, drones, and embedded AI will show on the balance sheet in 2028-2029. FPGA content in a robot can amount to several hundred dollars per robot, he said, representing huge growth potential.
“My hope is that [this time next year] we will have a very solid humming system, an independent company running at full performance and delivering the results,” Hussain said.
Altera’s branding, sidelined as part of Intel’s PSG group, is coming back, with a refreshed logo in a new color and without the Intel i.
“People think Altera is dead,” Hussain said. “So now when we go back, they think, oh, you guys are still around! So we have a lot of work still to do.”
Intel headquarters, visible from the windows of Hussain’s fifth-floor office, is partially blocked by trees.
“We just need those trees to grow a little bit,” he joked.

articles.title: Reliance Retail launches AJIO Beauty, expands footprint in personal care segment
articles.text:
Reliance Retail launches AJIO Beauty, expands footprint in personal care segment
The new platform combines the fashion-first digital reach of AJIO with the beauty expertise of Tira, the company's omnichannel beauty venture, to create what it described as a one-stop destination for skincare, makeup, haircare, fragrances, bath and personal care products.
Reliance Retail on Tuesday announced the launch of AJIO Beauty platform to strengthen its presence in the fast-growing beauty and personal care segment as part of its broader fashion and lifestyle ecosystem.
The new platform combines the fashion-first digital reach of AJIO with the beauty expertise of Tira, the company's omnichannel beauty venture, to create what it described as a one-stop destination for skincare, makeup, haircare, fragrances, bath and personal care products.
AJIO Beauty will offer products across value, bridge-to-luxury, premium and luxury categories, featuring more than 1,500 Indian and global brands, said a statement from Reliance Retail.
The platform will deliver to over 19,000 pin codes across the country, the company said, adding that a range of beauty products would also be available on AJIO Rush, its quick-commerce delivery service, in select cities.
"With AJIO Beauty, we are extending AJIO's fashion-first philosophy into the beauty space, creating a destination where customers can discover products that complement their individuality and lifestyle," said a spokesperson.
The company said the platform is designed to move beauty shopping beyond a purely transactional experience by incorporating trend discovery, curated routines, ingredient-led recommendations and personalised suggestions for users.
The launch comes as Reliance Retail continues to scale its lifestyle portfolio, integrating its fashion and beauty businesses to serve what it called the "evolving needs" of Indian consumers.
Reliance Retail, a subsidiary of Reliance Retail Ventures Limited (RRVL), the holding company of all the retail companies under the RIL (Reliance Industries) group, operates an omnichannel network of 20,169 stores.
RRVL recorded a gross revenue of Rs 3.70 lakh crore for the year ended March 31, 2026.

articles.title: Puces M6 et M7, MacBook Neo, écran tactile : Apple prépare un raz-de-marée pour sa gamme Mac
articles.text:
Puces M6 et M7, MacBook Neo, écran tactile : Apple prépare un raz-de-marée pour sa gamme Mac
Face à la demande en intelligence artificielle, Apple prépare une mise à jour de sa gamme Mac. Entre nouvelles puces et évolutions d'affichage, la marque ajuste sa stratégie malgré des contraintes de production.
Selon Bloomberg, Apple s'apprête à faire évoluer l'ensemble de ses ordinateurs personnels d'ici l'année prochaine. Portés par un regain d'intérêt auprès des utilisateurs exécutant des agents d'intelligence artificielle en local, les Mac enregistrent des prévisions de ventes en hausse pour la troisième année consécutive.
La transition doit débuter à l'automne avec un MacBook Pro de 14 pouces d'entrée de gamme équipé d'une puce M6 (nom de code J804), ainsi qu'une révision de l'iMac (J833 et J834), dont la dernière version remonte à deux ans. Le développement de ces appareils est finalisé, mais leur commercialisation est prévue pour le deuxième semestre.
Oled et écran tactile au programme des modèles haut de gamme
Parmi les évolutions prévues, la firme de Cupertino travaille sur de nouveaux MacBook Pro haut de gamme de 14 et 16 pouces (K114 et K116). Ces modèles introduiront deux nouveautés pour la famille des Mac : une dalle Oled offrant des couleurs plus chatoyantes et un écran tactile.
Actuellement testées sous macOS 27.1, ces machines devraient sortir entre la fin d'année et le début d'année prochaine. Elles intégreront les puces M5 Pro et M5 Max, avant une future génération dotée des puces M7 Pro et M7 Max planifiée entre fin 2027 et début 2028.
Révisions pour le MacBook Air, la gamme Neo et le reste du catalogue
Le MacBook Air de 13 et 15 pouces (J913 et J915) connaîtra également une mise à jour d'ici le début d'année prochaine, en conservant un design proche du modèle actuel, en attendant une version Oled envisagée pour 2028. En parallèle, un nouveau MacBook Pro 14 pouces (K104) tirera parti d'un nouveau châssis et d'une puce M7 standard l'année prochaine.
Du côté de l'entrée de gamme, le MacBook Neo, lancé en mars, fait l'objet de tests avec une puce A19 Pro révisée et davantage de mémoire vive (12 Go). De nouvelles déclinaisons de couleurs sont prévues pour ce modèle accessible. Dans un avenir plus lointain, Apple prévoit le passage à l'Oled pour l’iMac, ainsi que des mises à jour des Mac mini et Mac Studio.
Des tensions sur les composants et des prix ajustés
Apple fait face à une pénurie de puces mémoire qui perturbe ses chaînes de fabrication, en particulier pour les Mac mini et Mac Studio, très prisés par les utilisateurs d’agents IA. Les délais de livraison pour certaines configurations dépassent les trois mois.
Pour faire face à ces coûts et à la gestion des stocks, la marque a augmenté les tarifs de l'ensemble de ses ordinateurs en juin. Le MacBook Neo est ainsi passé de 699 € à 799 €, le MacBook Air 13 pouces de 1199 € à 1349 €, tandis que certaines configurations de stockage et mémoire vive disparaissent. En parallèle, l'entreprise tente de diversifier son empreinte industrielle en étendant la production du Mac mini à Houston pour le marché domestique.

articles.title: Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 : la meilleure montre connectée de Samsung s’attaque à Garmin
articles.text:
La synthèse parfaite de la montre de sport et de la montre connectée : cet idéal, tout le monde s’y est essayé, personne n’y est parvenu. Ça n’empêche pas Samsung sur le métier de remettre son ouvrage. Pas cent fois, mais deux. Après une première version de la Galaxy Watch Ultra lancée en marge des JO de Paris 2024, voici venu le temps de la successeure : la Galaxy Watch Ultra 2, la montre de sport ultime de Samsung.
Plus agréable au poignet
Les principales critiques concernant la première Watch Ultra de Samsung concernaient en partie un design massif, son poids conséquent et une certaine lourdeur au poignet pouvant rendre la montre inconfortable au bout de plusieurs heures d’effort physique. Pour l’Ultra 2, Samsung a décidé d’adresser toutes les critiques et a fait évoluer son modèle. Le design général qui joue sur l’ambivalence entre boîtier carré et lunette ronde est reconduit, mais l’épaisseur de la montre s’est considérablement réduite. Elle mesure désormais 10,7 mm, contre 12,1 mm sur l’Ultra originale, soit un gain de 12%. Au poignet, la différence est immédiatement perceptible et donne à la nouvelle version une impression de confort bienvenue.
Cet effort d’amincissement se retrouve aussi sur le bracelet. Oubliez l’épais plastique de la précédente version. L’Ultra 2 propose un accessoire plus fin de 1 mm, mais surtout plus souple et plus agréable au toucher. En plus d’être 25% plus léger que le précédent, il est aussi aéré selon le procédé dit « Air Pocket », qui existe aussi sur la Galaxy Watch 9. Autrement dit, la gestion de la sueur s’en trouve améliorée, tout comme la précision des capteurs. Concrètement, les dimensions de la Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 de Samsung sont les suivantes : 47,4 x 47,1 x 10,7 pour un poids contenu de 61,5 g.
Enfin, la Watch Ultra 2 accompagne ce design soigné d’une robustesse certifiée. Sa structure en titane est une chose, mais les certifications IP69K et EN13319 (pour de la plongée jusqu’à 10 m) complètent joliment le tableau d’une montre taillée pour les sports outdoor et qui se veut la rivale d’une Fenix 8 Pro de Garmin.
L’écran le plus lumineux au monde
Le design de l’Ultra 2 est sublimé par un écran Super AMOLED qui attire immédiatement l’œil. Celui-ci est légèrement plus grand que sur la précédente version (1,52 pouce contre 1,47), mais il est surtout nettement plus lumineux. Avec un pic attendu à 5 000 nits, Samsung parle officiellement de « l’écran de montre le plus lumineux au monde ».
Cette luminosité devrait avoir des conséquences heureuses pour la lisibilité de la montre en plein soleil. Ce n’était déjà pas un souci pour Samsung, ça le sera encore moins. Mais attendons le test complet pour en juger.
Grosse batterie, charge rapide : les fondamentaux du smartphone sur une montre
Si extérieurement les changements sont notables, à l’intérieur c’est encore plus net. Samsung a complètement repensé le hardware de sa montre haut de gamme. Avec une nouvelle puce pour commencer, la Snapdragon Wear Elite qui est présentée par Qualcomm comme le meilleur choix possible pour les montres connectées et qui affiche une meilleure efficience énergétique en plus d’une précision accrue sur le GPS.
Concrètement, Samsung communique sur des gains de performance de l’ordre de 32% sur le CPU et 19% sur le GPU.
Ce n’est pas tout. Ce changement de puce s’accompagne d’une partie batterie plus musclée. L’Ultra 2 embarque un accumulateur de 800 mAh (contre 590 mAh) auparavant. Dans les faits, cela correspond à un usage de plus de 20 h en continu avec le GPS et à environ 16 h en GPX. Si ces données sont confirmées par le test, elles feraient de la montre de sport de Samsung l’une des plus sérieuses en matière d’autonomie.
Mais plus que sur la capacité de la batterie, là où Samsung pourrait se distinguer cette année, c’est sur la recharge. De manière générale, les montres de sport ne sont pas connues pour leur vélocité une fois branchées. La marque coréenne veut se démarquer sur ce point en apportant son savoir-faire issu du smartphone. Ainsi, l’Ultra 2 est dotée d’une fonctionnalité de charge rapide qui lui permet de récupérer 40% de sa batterie en 30 min. Pratique quand on veut aussi la garder la nuit pour analyser son sommeil et que les moments de charge sont comptés.
Une montre connectée pour le trail ?
Ce qui va distinguer aussi Samsung d’un Garmin ou d’un Suunto, c’est la partie logicielle. La nouvelle version de Google Health apporte son lot de nouveautés, que nous avons pu vous faire découvrir dans la présentation de la Galaxy Watch 9.
Mais en plus des scores de cœur, de vitalité, de sommeil de l’indice Fitness ou de la protection de l’audition et de la charge cardio, l’Ultra 2 va bénéficier de fonctionnalités spécifiques. Trois d’entre elles élèvent particulièrement le niveau :
- Un mode trail avec cartographie intégrée qui affiche en plus du dénivelé des rappels d’hydratation en fonction des données récoltées.
- Une application plongée développée avec le spécialiste Mares (essai gratuit puis abonnement)
- Un mode vélo plus poussé qui intègre puissance, cadence et vitesse issus du capteur de puissance, en temps réel.
Enfin, l’arrivée de l’Ultra 2 est aussi pour Samsung l’occasion de revoir son partenariat avec Strava, la plateforme de référence des sportifs. En plus d’offrir un essai de deux mois au mode Premium de l’application lors de l’achat d’une montre, Samsung évoque une meilleure synchronisation entre les données des deux plateformes. Il devrait donc y avoir un peu moins de différences entre les données recueillies par la montre et celles recalculées par la plateforme.
Prix et disponibilité de la Galaxy Watch Ultra 2
Avec sa nouvelle montre connectée pour les sports outdoor, Samsung tente à nouveau ce mariage si délicat entre montre de sport affirmée et capable de résister à de grosses séances et des courses intenses et montre connectée/plaisir. Seul un test au long cours permettrait de savoir si Samsung est allé un peu plus loin que la concurrence dans cette quête qui sur le papier semble presque impossible. En attendant, il convient d’apprécier les efforts réalisés par le fabricant pour répondre aux demandes des sportifs les plus exigeants. L’amélioration du GPS et de l’autonomie étaient nécessaires pour jouer dans la même division que Garmin & co.
L’ajout d’un mode Trail et de petites fonctionnalités telles que la charge rapide pourraient aussi peser.
En attendant, Samsung commercialise sa Watch Ultra 2 en une seule taille (47 mm) et en deux coloris, noir titane ou argent. Contrairement à la Watch 9 qui propose deux niveaux de connectivité, la plus haut de gamme des montres de Samsung affiche d’emblée 4G et Bluetooth. Son prix : 749 euros.

articles.title: L’industrie de l’IA menace-t-elle de s’effondrer ? Le problème d’efficacité qui inquiète tout le secteur
articles.text:
L’intelligence artificielle (IA) générative devait devenir moins chère à mesure qu’elle grandirait. C’est tout l’inverse qui se produit, et la facture commence à peser lourd, jusque chez les géants de la tech.
Depuis des années, les entreprises d’IA vendent la même promesse aux investisseurs : plus un modèle est gros, plus il devient puissant. C’est ce qu’on appelle les « lois d’échelle ». Mais sur le terrain, cette course au gigantisme commence à coûter très cher.
Un problème d’échelle
Quand un service de streaming ou une application mobile gagne des millions d’utilisateurs supplémentaires, le coût de chaque nouvel utilisateur diminue. C’est ce qu’on appelle une économie d’échelle, et c'est exactement ce que recherchent les investisseurs : plus l’entreprise grossit, plus elle devient rentable.
Problème, IA génératives comme ChatGPT ou Claude fonctionnent dans le sens inverse. Plus on leur soumet de texte à traiter, plus elles réclament de mémoire et de temps de calcul. Et cette hausse n’est pas proportionnelle, puisqu’elle s’accélère à mesure que les volumes augmentent. Ainsi, doubler la quantité de texte à analyser peut largement plus que doubler la facture.
Ce défaut technique se répercute directement sur le portefeuille des entreprises clientes, car la plupart des contrats facturent l’usage de l’IA au volume traité, le fameux token. Résultat, la note grimpe avec l’intensité d’utilisation, sans que la valeur réellement produite pour l’entreprise suive au même rythme.
Les impacts sont déjà concrets
Cette inefficacité a des répercussions colossales. Car pour faire tourner leurs modèles, les géants de l’IA achètent aujourd’hui jusqu’à 70 % de l’offre mondiale de mémoire informatique haut de gamme. Conséquence directe, les prix des disques durs, des ordinateurs et des smartphones s’envolent, et la tendance ne semble malheureusement pas près de s'arrêter.
Et bien sûr, l'impact énergétique de cette dynamique est désastreux. Pour absorber une telle demande, la capacité des data centers américains pourrait être multipliée par huit dans les prochaines années, au point que certaines entreprises envisagent de recycler des réacteurs d’avion pour produire assez d’électricité. Un défi d’autant plus difficile à relever que les progrès du matériel informatique ralentissent : les composants ont atteint des limites physiques qui freinent leur miniaturisation.
Dans ce contexte, la rentabilité du secteur reste un immense point d’interrogation. De quoi un peu plus alimenter les craintes d’une bulle spéculative autour de l’IA, un secteur dans lequel des pans entiers de l’économie ont massivement investi…
Les lois d’échelle décrivent une relation empirique entre trois variables : la taille du modèle (nombre de paramètres), la quantité de données d’entraînement et la puissance de calcul utilisée. En pratique, elles indiquent que, quand on augmente ces ressources, les performances s’améliorent de manière assez prévisible sur certains indicateurs (perplexité, scores de benchmarks). Le point clé est que le gain est souvent marginal : chaque “palier” de performance coûte beaucoup plus cher que le précédent. Elles concernent surtout l’entraînement, mais elles poussent aussi à déployer des modèles plus gros, donc plus coûteux à faire tourner. Enfin, elles ne garantissent pas que les gains se traduisent automatiquement en valeur métier ou en baisse des coûts.
Lorsqu’un modèle génère ou analyse du texte, il doit traiter une séquence de tokens et maintenir un « contexte » en mémoire pour produire une réponse cohérente. Dans l’architecture Transformer utilisée par la plupart des grands modèles, le mécanisme d’attention a un coût qui tend à croître de façon quadratique avec la longueur du contexte (en simplifiant : plus il y a de tokens, plus il y a de relations à calculer). Cela augmente à la fois le temps de calcul (GPU) et la quantité de mémoire nécessaire, ce qui se répercute directement sur la facture. Même quand des optimisations existent (attention plus efficace, compression de contexte), elles ne font pas disparaître le problème pour les usages à très gros volumes. Résultat : allonger les prompts, multiplier les documents à ingérer ou augmenter les fenêtres de contexte fait grimper les coûts très vite.
Un token est une unité de texte utilisée pour mesurer l’entrée (prompt) et la sortie (réponse) d’un modèle ; ce n’est pas exactement un mot, mais plutôt un morceau de mot ou de ponctuation. La plupart des API d’IA facturent séparément les tokens entrants et sortants, parfois avec un tarif plus élevé pour des modèles plus performants ou des fenêtres de contexte plus grandes. Ce mode de facturation relie directement le coût à l’intensité d’usage : plus on automatise, plus on ingère de documents, plus on génère de texte, plus la dépense grimpe mécaniquement. Il peut aussi pénaliser les cas où la valeur produite ne croît pas au même rythme que le volume de tokens (ex. réponses longues, reformulations, itérations). Sans garde-fous (quotas, routage vers des modèles plus petits, cache de réponses), une adoption rapide peut dépasser les budgets prévisionnels.

articles.title: Desmantelan red de estafas bancarias en España: tenían una base de datos de 500.000 ciudadanos
articles.text:
Una red de estafas bancarias que operaba con una base de datos de 500.000 ciudadanos con información personal y financiera robada fue desarticulada en España por la Guardia Civil.
La organización, integrada por 18 personas, 10 hombres y ocho mujeres de entre 23 y 43 años, utilizaba las técnicas de smishing y phishing para suplantar la identidad de entidades bancarias a través de mensajes de texto.
PUBLICIDAD
El caso comenzó a tomar forma en 2024 a partir de la denuncia de un ciudadano que perdió cerca de 30.000 euros tras recibir una falsa comunicación de su banco.
La operación, denominada Fragmenta, saldó 13 detenidos y cinco investigados en Madrid, Palma de Mallorca, Valencia y Toledo, y permitió identificar cerca de 2.000 posibles víctimas.
PUBLICIDAD
Cuál fue el principal hallazgo de la investigación
El hallazgo más revelador de la operación no fue el dinero ni los dispositivos incautados, sino el archivo digital que sostenía toda la operación: una base de datos con información personal y bancaria de aproximadamente 500.000 personas.
Ese repositorio funcionó como el insumo central del esquema, ya que permitió a la organización seleccionar objetivos, personalizar los mensajes fraudulentos y escalar el volumen de ataques con una precisión que habría sido imposible sin acceso previo a los datos.
PUBLICIDAD
La Guardia Civil no precisó en su comunicado el origen de esa base de datos ni el modo en que fue obtenida, aunque su magnitud sugiere que la red no actuó de forma aislada, sino que accedió a información filtrada de fuentes externas o la acumuló a través de sucesivas campañas de captura de credenciales.
La investigación continúa abierta y no se descarta que aparezcan nuevos afectados a medida que se analice el archivo.
La Guardia Civil destacó que la investigación exigió un trabajo de “inteligencia financiera y análisis tecnológico” por la complejidad de la arquitectura que sostenía la red.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo atacaba esta red de estafas
La cadena de ataque seguía una arquitectura de dos etapas diseñada para maximizar la tasa de éxito.
En la primera, la organización enviaba de forma masiva mensajes SMS que aparentaban proceder de entidades bancarias legítimas.
El objetivo era dirigir a las víctimas hacia páginas web fraudulentas donde introducían sus credenciales de banca electrónica.
En la segunda fase, los integrantes del grupo contactaban telefónicamente con las víctimas haciéndose pasar por empleados del banco para obtener los códigos de verificación, los llamados OTP o one-time passwords, necesarios para autorizar operaciones.
PUBLICIDAD
Con ese acceso, realizaban transferencias del dinero disponible y solicitaban préstamos preconcedidos u otros productos financieros a nombre de los afectados.
La organización operaba con identidades falsas, cuentas abiertas mediante terceros y transferencias inmediatas entre distintas entidades, pero el elemento que más dificultó el rastreo fue una infraestructura tecnológica distribuida en varios países, cuya localización no fue detallada en el comunicado oficial.
PUBLICIDAD
Una vez obtenido el control de las cuentas, los fondos se dispersaban a través de numerosas cuentas bancarias para entorpecer su seguimiento y blanquear el dinero.
Cómo protegerse ante intentos de estafas de este tipo
La Guardia Civil recordó que las entidades bancarias no solicitan por teléfono, SMS ni correo electrónico las claves de acceso, contraseñas o códigos de verificación de sus clientes.
PUBLICIDAD
Ante cualquier comunicación sospechosa, el cuerpo recomendó no facilitar datos personales o bancarios, acceder a la banca electrónica únicamente a través de los canales oficiales y contactar directamente con la entidad para verificar la autenticidad del mensaje.
También aconsejó revisar de forma periódica los movimientos de las cuentas y comunicar de inmediato cualquier operación no autorizada.
Por otra parte, es aconsejable notificar a las autoridades si se sospecha haber sido víctima de un caso similar, a fin de que puedan avanzar las investigaciones.
PUBLICIDAD
